newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end sharply weaker with U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end sharply weaker with U.S. market.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended sharlply weaker on Thursday, following a selloff in U.S. bonds amid heightened fears of a hike in U.S. short-term interest rates.

Stronger U.S. retail sales data on Thursday prompted concerns that rising inflation may have to be quelled by the U.S. Federal Reserve. February sales rose 0.8 percent, compared to a 0.6 percent gain forecast by economists.

Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.85 to C$109.57 to yield 7.183 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark, which fell 28/32 to yield 6.95 percent. The spread between the two narrowed to 23 basis points from 24 at Wednesday's close.
